## Report

`tests/unit/test_path_injection_guards.py::test_rerun_502_body_has_no_exception_detail` FAILS on current `origin/main` (reproduced standalone at 43ecfa8f27, and independently at 9bdb22f5887 before that):

```
AttributeError: 'types.SimpleNamespace' object has no attribute 'headers'
src/rebar/review_bot/app.py:101: in _request_token
    header_token = request.headers.get(TOKEN_HEADER, "").strip()
```

## Mechanism (unconfirmed — for the investigation to prove)

`_request_token` (`src/rebar/review_bot/app.py:101`) reads `request.headers` unconditionally. The header path was added for ticket 66af (accept the token via header, keeping the query param for legacy Gerrit webhooks whose `webhooks.config` has not been re-pushed). The test constructs its request as a `types.SimpleNamespace` that predates that change and carries no `headers` attribute, so the attribute read raises before any assertion runs.

Whether the correct fix is to make `_request_token` tolerate a header-less request object, or to update the test's fake to match the real request contract, is EXACTLY the question the investigation must answer — a header-less request may be a real shape in production (some ASGI/test clients) or may be purely a test artifact. Do not assume.

## Why it matters

This is red on main. It reds the `Verified` CI gate for anyone whose change touches this suite, and it is a SECURITY-adjacent guard: the test exists to prove a 502 body carries no exception detail (path-injection guard). A guard test that errors before asserting proves nothing — the guarantee it is supposed to pin is currently unverified.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] The root cause is proven, with a cited mechanism, not guessed — the stale `types.SimpleNamespace` request double at tests/unit/test_path_injection_guards.py:163-166, left behind when ticket 66af (4e8c83c833) widened `_request_token` (src/rebar/review_bot/app.py:101) to read `request.headers` FIRST.
- [x] It is established and stated whether a header-less request is a REAL production shape or a test-only artifact, with evidence — **TEST ARTIFACT, not a real shape.** starlette's `HTTPConnection.headers` (requests.py:132-136) is an unconditional property; deleting `headers` from an ASGI scope raises `KeyError`, NEVER `AttributeError` — so the observed `AttributeError` is only producible by an object that is not a `Request` at all. A real request with zero caller headers still carries an empty `Headers`. FastAPI binds a `Request`-annotated param behind an `isinstance` gate (fastapi/dependencies/utils.py:711), whose only alternative is `WebSocket` — also an `HTTPConnection`, also with `.headers`. Full evidence in the Phase 1 RCA comment.
- [x] The test passes on a clean tree and actually exercises its original assertion (a 502 body containing no exception detail), not merely stops erroring — proven by defect-seeded mutation: adding `"detail": str(exc)` to the 502 body returns the test to RED, naming the leaked string in the failure output. The ORIGINAL test could not have caught that; it raised before its first assert.
- [x] A regression test fails against the pre-fix code and passes after — two mutations of the production path each return it to RED (leak the exception detail -> assertion diff; stub out the `X-Rebar-Token` header read -> 401), and it is GREEN with src/rebar/review_bot/app.py byte-identical to main. No production code changed.
- [x] The fix lands on main through Gerrit with LLM-Review +1 and Verified +1 — change 1481 (https://rebar.solutions.navateam.com/c/rebar/+/1481): LLM-Review+1 (PASS) and Verified+1 (Actions run 31167914711, SUCCESS), 0 unresolved comments, MERGED 2026-08-07 10:17:28 as origin/main aaf71639b8.
